item.title: AI Agent Memory Statistics (October 2026)
item.description:
These AI agent memory statistics were collected on 2026-10-20 by aiagentmemory.org from the GitHub, PyPI and npm APIs. claude-mem has the most GitHub stars (101,934), Mem0 has the most PyPI downloads (2,020,516 last month), and Hindsight ranks fourth on stars and second on PyPI downloads. Hindsight had the top BEAM 10M score in MemTensor’s same-model OmniMemEval run (59.75, checked 2026-10-12).

All GitHub and download numbers on this page were collected 2026-10-20 between about 18:45 and 18:56 UTC, by us, from public APIs. We’re the primary source for them. Benchmark scores are not ours: they’re copied from the vendors who ran them, with who ran each one. The exact calls are in the Methodology section.

item.title: Agent Memory Leaderboard: Benchmarks and Scores
item.description:
There is no official agent memory leaderboard. The benchmark authors (LongMemEval, LoCoMo, BEAM) publish datasets, not rankings. The leaderboards you can find are run by memory vendors: agentmemorybenchmark.ai by Vectorize, the company that makes Hindsight; OmniMemEval by MemTensor, the company that makes MemOS; and score pages from Mem0, Zep, Honcho and past.dev.

So every ranking has an owner, and every score depends on the answer model, judge and token budget that owner chose. This page lists where the leaderboards are, what each benchmark measures, the published scores with who reported each one, and how to read them. Everything was checked on the source pages on 12 October 2026. For GitHub stars and PyPI and npm download counts for 23 memory projects, see AI agent memory statistics.

item.title: LLM Memory Evaluation: Benchmarks for Agent Memory
item.description:
LLM memory evaluation means testing whether a model or agent can recall, update and reason over information from earlier sessions. The standard benchmarks are LoCoMo and LongMemEval, with MemoryAgentBench and BEAM as harder, newer tests. Each feeds a long chat history to the system, then asks questions only that history can answer.

The tests differ in what they stress: plain recall, time, changed facts, forgetting, or scale. Picking the wrong one tells you little about your use case. Two 2026 benchmarks, FEB-30 and Bemula, go further and score the memory store itself rather than the answer. This page covers what each benchmark measures, how it’s scored, and how to run one yourself.
